# Photo fixtures

`tests/hdr-jpeg.helpers.ts` generates original synthetic gray, white, HDR and color reference charts at runtime. These generated reference pixels are dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0, like the export gain-map vectors. User photographs require explicit repository-inclusion permission; the research set below is the authorized exception.

These files are used only by automated tests. Irodori never loads them into a user's library automatically.

The shared [repository asset layout](../../assets/README.md) places application
resources under `assets/app/`, test and benchmark images under
`assets/tests/images/`, and numeric fixtures under `assets/tests/references/`.
Migration of all existing assets and their consumers is tracked as unchecked
backlog item #35. Until that migration, existing fixture paths below remain valid;
new assets use the shared layout. Move the manifests, attribution and this privacy
guidance alongside the assets during migration.

For additional source photographs, follow
[obtaining missing photographic inputs](../../assets/README.md#obtaining-missing-photographic-inputs).

## Color-model reference vectors

`color-model-reference.json` contains 110 synthetic signed SDR/HDR color vectors and 770
Saturation/Vibrance candidate outputs generated by
`scripts/research/color-reference.py` with 80-digit Decimal arithmetic. The reference derives
RGB/XYZ matrices from sRGB/Rec.2020 primary chromaticities and D65, uses the published forward
Oklab matrices from [CSS Color 4, 2026-10-22](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-css-color-4-20261022/#color-conversion-code),
and independently solves the inverse matrices. The fixture records its generator hash. The
original generator and generated numeric vectors are dedicated to the public domain under
CC0-1.0. There are no photographs or copied third-party program files in this fixture.

`color-intensity-reference.json` contains 924 independent CIE 1976 Lab/D65 intensity
vectors from `scripts/research/cie-color-reference.py`, using the same independently
derived primary matrices and 80-digit Decimal arithmetic. D65 is deliberate; this
is not the D50 CSS Lab convention. Both generator hashes are recorded in the fixture.
It covers signed values, near black, 16× reference white, both working primaries,
and the full Saturation/Vibrance control range. The original numeric data and generator
are CC0-1.0. These are numerical references; photographic appearance and performance
need separate acceptance evidence.

`creative-color-reference.json` contains 2,520 binary64-input and 2,520 Float32-input
independent mixer/intensity/three-way grading vectors from
`scripts/research/creative-color-reference.py`. Float32 rounding happens before the
oracle evaluates GPU inputs, keeping input quantization separate from kernel error. The Decimal80
oracle independently derives the primary matrices, finds angular hue intervals,
solves their chord coefficients and reconstructs complete XYZ/RGB. It does not import
application algorithms or constants. It records both generator hashes and covers both
working primaries, eight reference colors, signed values, neutral protection,
1e-12…16× exposure, range extremes and tonal overlap/balance endpoints. Separate
stage and fused outputs use the fixed numerical limits in
[the processing contract](../../docs/features/color-mixer-grading-processing.md).
The original generator and numeric data are CC0-1.0; photographic quality, frame
integration and performance require separate acceptance evidence.

`tone-curve-reference.json` contains ten synthetic curve cases and independently
evaluated Decimal80 Hermite-basis samples from `scripts/research/tone-curve-reference.py`.
It uses exact binary64 API inputs, independent endpoint/interior derivative evaluation,
and rational tails. Cases include identity, matte, flat endpoints, intentionally
nonmonotone curves, sixteen points and closely spaced points near HDR bounds.
It also includes dense exact Float32 image inputs and composed Master/RGB references
in sRGB and Rec.2020, using independently evaluated rational matrices and CIE Lab/D65.
The generator hash and source reference are embedded. This original generator and
numeric fixture are CC0-1.0; no third-party implementation or photograph is included.

`crop-reference.json` contains 216 independently evaluated Decimal80 geometry cases
and 1,512 source-coordinate vectors from `scripts/research/crop-reference.py`.
It derives sine/cosine with Taylor series, fits by corner-search bisection and undoes
quarter rotations one at a time; it imports no application geometry. The cases cover
all quarter turns, both angle limits, fractional centers, aspect locks, non-square
images and 32768-pixel source edges. The fixture records the generator SHA-256.
This original numeric data and generator are CC0-1.0; no photograph is included.

`crop-filter-reference.json` contains eight original 9×9 Float32 scenes and 648
independent Decimal80 reconstruction vectors from `scripts/research/crop-filter-reference.py`.
It evaluates four Hermite basis functions, premultiplied nonnegative alpha-edge
interpolation and border extension without importing the application kernel. It covers
linear/quadratic ramps, signed/HDR values, patterned detail, transparency, low coverage
and dark constants. The generator records its SHA-256 and compares bilinear, Catmull-Rom
and normalized Lanczos3 on declared sinusoid/step/quadrant/diagonal/impulse/checker charts.
The checker reference is its explicit analytic continuation, not recovered detail from
an unknown photograph. Original code and numeric data are CC0-1.0; no photograph or
third-party filter implementation is copied.

## Reproducible photographic inputs

The project owner reaffirmed on 2026-10-29 that real photographs used for testing
or benchmarking must be saved in the GitHub repository. Store new selected originals
under `assets/tests/images/` unchanged, with SHA-256 hashes, capture/source provenance and an explicit
permission or license notice. Preserve removable-card files and verify their
hashes before and after copying. Tests resolve fixtures relative to the checkout;
private paths and removable cards must not be their only source. This rule does
not grant a general license to other photographs on a card.

Verify that every photographic benchmark input is tracked and included in the
benchmark's commit. A copy in the working directory, an ignored directory or a
local archive does not satisfy this requirement; never assume it will remain
available on this machine or another checkout.

Generated charts remain reproducible from their committed generators. Generated
proof crops, screenshots, caches and benchmark measurements remain ignored
artifacts; regenerate them from the retained originals and frozen settings.

The [privacy-reviewed Sony fog/animal-fur dataset](../../assets/tests/images/raw/sony-zv-1a/fog-dogs/README.md)
is stored in the shared asset tree. Its unchanged `DSC03280.ARW` supports native
RAW, fur/detail and resource/presentation checks; ISO 400 does not supply high-ISO
acceptance. Its notice records source integrity, repository-inclusion permission
and the completed visual/metadata privacy review.

The same shared tree also retains the genuine
[three-frame outdoor bracket](../../assets/tests/images/raw/sony-zv-1a/forest-bracket/README.md)
and the requested [carpet/paper ISO sequence](../../assets/tests/images/raw/sony-zv-1a/carpet-high-iso/README.md).
Each set has unchanged originals, capture facts, hashes, privacy review and a
separate inclusion notice. The carpet frames are approximately exposure-matched
comparisons with actual Program AE/AF-S/Auto WB; the lower-ISO frame is not
calibrated clean truth. Photographic and processing acceptance remain separate.

### Privacy review before committing

Before adding an image to Git or uploading it to GitHub, visually inspect the
full image and any embedded previews for personal information: identifiable
people, private interiors, documents, screens, addresses and vehicle plates.
Inspect embedded EXIF, XMP and IPTC metadata as well, including GPS coordinates,
names, contact details and camera or lens serial numbers. Check the fixture's
filename and provenance notice for accidental disclosure too. Repository-inclusion
permission and licensing do not replace this privacy review.

If a candidate exposes personal information, keep it out of Git and choose a
safe, appropriately licensed replacement. Preserve source originals unchanged;
do not silently redact or strip metadata from an image already used for a
measurement. Rerun affected benchmarks with the reviewed replacement and retain
that exact input in the repository. Record completion of the privacy review in
the fixture's provenance notice without copying sensitive details into it.

## Sony research sequences

[research-sony](research-sony/README.md) contains fifteen unchanged Sony ZV-1A SD-card originals: one real three-frame HDR BRK capture and a twelve-frame noise burst. The user explicitly requested repository inclusion for reproducible benchmarks across Linux and Mac. Its manifest records provenance, per-file hashes, recording/capture facts and dimensions; its notice grants no general open-content license. This permission applies only to this set. Other private photographs and generated evidence remain outside Git.

## Observed starfield

[observed starfield](../../assets/tests/images/raster/eso/observed-starfield/README.md) retains the unchanged published
651 × 651 JPEG of ESO image `eso0106a`, with full **AURA** credit and CC BY 4.0
source/license links. Its manifest pins the download and byte hash. This processed
telescope U-band image supports bounded star-detail review; it is not Sony RAW,
radiometric truth or a clean/noisy pair. Generated variants retain visible credit
and identify their processing changes.

## Historical portrait research

The earlier portrait research inputs do not pass the updated privacy policy for
new acceptance inputs. Their unchanged local bytes, manifests, permission notices
and failed/successful historical measurements are preserved in ignored evidence;
the newly added untracked set was removed from the active fixture tree before any
feature commit. Prior publication does not override the current policy. Use
reviewed replacements for further acceptance and preserve their exact provenance.

## Sony ZV-1

`sony-zv1.ARW` is the unmodified **Sony ZV-1, 12-bit compressed, 3:2** sample (original filename `DSC00056.ARW`) published by [raw.pixls.us](https://raw.pixls.us/), record 4000, uploaded July 10, 2020.

- [Download source](https://raw.pixls.us/getfile.php/4000/nice/Sony%20-%20ZV-1%20-%2012bit%2012bit%20compressed%20%283%3A2%29.ARW)
- [Metadata](https://raw.pixls.us/getfile.php/4000/exif/DSC00056.ARW.exif.txt)
- License: [CC0 1.0 / public domain](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), as recorded in the site's repository catalog.
- SHA-256: `14c9d2912584a3ccc5cf10f554fbe495fc960c36758a14d7d858b36ac5ca88e2`

The fixture is committed so tests run offline. Embedded extraction is deliberately replaced with a failing dependency in the fallback test; LibRaw still decodes the real, unchanged camera file.

## Single-image detail references

`detail-reference.json` contains original CC0-1.0 Decimal80 vectors generated by
`scripts/research/detail-reference.py`, using the independent primary solver in
`color-reference.py`. It covers bounded NLM, protected luminance sharpening and
Float32 publication between stages, including alpha-zero hidden RGB, tiny alpha,
signed zero, dark/signed channels and at least 16× white. No application code or
third-party image is used. Source hashes are embedded in the fixture.

`detail-quality.json` uses original deterministic synthetic clean/noisy charts from
`scripts/research/detail-quality-reference.py` and `detail-candidates.py`. The
independent prefix-sum comparison retains known truth, entering pixels, output and
metrics. It includes flat/color noise, repeating texture, isoluminant edges, stars
and a merge-like noise boundary. These CC0-1.0 fixtures do not replace paired real
captures, photographic review or performance acceptance. See the predeclared
[operator gates](../../docs/features/detail-processing.md).

`tests/detail-frame.helpers.ts` generates additional original CC0-1.0 linear
frame data for adapter tests. It includes a nonzero view offset, backing padding,
signed/HDR RGB, partial/tiny alpha and explicit synthetic source references. No
third-party photograph or real catalog metadata is used. The layer tests preserve
the backing bytes, compare file/frame and native-tile output, and exercise metadata
and ownership; the independent numerical/quality references above remain required.

`tests/detail-preview.helpers.ts` creates original CC0-1.0 tiny PNGs and labelled
synthetic HDR working descriptors for worker/output-domain tests. The authored-HDR
descriptor exercises source-aware rendering; it is not a real gain-map JPEG or
camera calibration fixture. All files live in isolated temporary directories.

`tests/detail-preview-cache.helpers.ts` reuses those CC0-1.0 inputs through the
actual isolated worker and application preview cache. Its synthetic HDR descriptors
exercise retained source identity and output-domain routing; they never decode a
real RAW or gain-map JPEG. WB-dispatch coverage records the unfiltered source and
deliberately rejects the synthetic proposal. Recovery and corruption checks alter
only owned temporary cache files and preserve the input photograph/working source.

`tests/detail-export.helpers.ts` reuses the CC0-1.0 tiny PNG and synthetic prepared
HDR sources for worker/rendition tests. Paired inputs test independent linear-sRGB
and Rec.2020 filtering, not real gain-map JPEG decoding or camera calibration.
The real export worker encodes SDR JPEG and a small paired HDR JPEG from synthetic
prepared inputs; these are not real gain-map input decodes or round-trip acceptance.
Private job-policy tests deliberately seed processing options
without enabling public denoising edits/history. Corruption/recovery tests touch
only temporary derived files and retain original/working-source bytes.

`detail-export-cache` also uses a deliberately unavailable original decoder path
after acquiring verified leases, to prove that worker reuse does not re-decode or
filter twice. `detail-native-source` feeds a 19x17 filtered cache FD to the checked
shipping native helper and compares downstream point rendering with the CPU path.
Both preserve the original CC0-1.0 inputs and use isolated temporary directories;
neither supplies real-camera, native desktop or full-size performance acceptance.

`detail-comparison` reuses the same original CC0-1.0 PNG/prepared HDR sources for an
unfiltered Before baseline on the committed crop. `detail-comparison-ui` generates
original 4x3 constant float arrays in an isolated child frame, exercising real React
hooks with deliberately distinguishable mocked capabilities. These do not supply
photographic quality or actual Before/Split presenter acceptance.

`raster-spatial-comparison` generates original CC0-1.0 8x6 Float32 patterns, including
partial/zero alpha and padded backing storage, in an isolated child frame. It
exercises the actual raster presenter/worker and tiny WebGL rendering with distinct
Before/After sources. Controlled reply/fence delays preserve actual computation;
injected capability/link failures exercise rejection and cleanup. These synthetic
inputs do not establish photographic quality, application wiring, HDR/native
pairing or full-size performance acceptance.

`hdr-spatial-comparison` generates original CC0-1.0 8x6 Float32 capture/authored-HDR
patterns with zero alpha in an isolated child frame. Blob capabilities feed the
real upload worker, mip shader and HDR presenter. Delayed message delivery/fences,
damaged temporary bytes, a constrained synthetic resource policy and simulated
float16 recovery unavailability exercise lifecycle/refusal paths. Authored SDR
uses its independent primary elsewhere; these synthetic HDR descriptors do not
decode a camera RAW or gain-map JPEG or establish photographic/native acceptance.

`native-cpu-comparison` uses original CC0-1.0 Float32 patterns, including a 7x129
three-strip input, and the existing 19x17 prepared-cache fixture. The checked native
helper supplies real bytes; a separate protocol child supplies controlled close
delays only. `native-cpu-comparison-ui` uses original 8x6 arrays with partial/zero
alpha in an isolated child frame. A test-only bridge forwards specific operations
to the real controller without changing production IPC. Independent CPU output
checks native bytes; an independently populated canvas checks browser bitmap
normalization. No real photograph or user library is accessed.

`hdr-cpu-comparison-ui` reuses original CC0-1.0 8x6 Float32 patterns with partial/zero
alpha for actual native and JavaScript CPU presenters. The test transport supplies
native capabilities or blob Range responses; real hash validation, worker rendering
and canvas presentation remain active. Independent CPU bytes and browser-normalized
references verify Before/Split, point edits and range overlays. `hdr-sample` uses
original tiny Float32 planes for paired observer and shared-buffer ownership checks.
These fixtures do not provide photographic, production IPC or desktop acceptance.

`detail-comparison-mask` reuses the original CC0-1.0 19x17 prepared HDR fixture.
It checks actual shipping native mask bytes against independent CPU analysis,
Before/After capability lineage and cache-pin ownership. Existing 8x6 CPU/GPU
comparison fixtures now also probe original-frame mask admission. These checks do
not decode a camera RAW, exercise production comparison IPC or accept full-size
photographic/performance behavior.

`detail-application-ui` creates an original CC0-1.0 deterministic opaque 19x17
noisy PNG. It drives production UI, MCP and comparison IPC and reads actual canvas
pixels for original Before/Split equality. Its restart and keyboard/layout cases
use isolated hidden profiles. `detail-edit-export` uses the existing original
17x11 CC0-1.0 PNG from `exportFixture`, real frozen edits and the built export
worker, including foreground cancellation/retry. These fixtures establish public
integration rather than photographic, actual HDR application or full-size
performance acceptance.

## Export resize references

`export-resize-reference.json` contains original CC0-1.0 Decimal80 direct
2D Lanczos3 convolution vectors generated by
`scripts/research/export-resize-reference.py`, without application imports.
Seven cases cover fractional signed/HDR paired channels, both one-pixel axes,
legacy reduction, exact identity, one unchanged axis and constants. Tests verify
the generator hash and fixed `2e-6 + 2e-5 * abs(reference)` Float32 tolerance.
Regenerate with the Python script and format the JSON with Prettier.

`export-enlargement` adds original tiny PNG/float fields, actual JPEG output,
foreground retry, resource refusal and independent ISO reconstruction. Its paired
fixture has a constant authored Rec.2020 HDR field and an independent PNG primary;
it exercises the production rendering/packaging adapter without a gain-map import
or camera decoder. `export-enlargement-gpu` uses an original 8x6 synthetic capture
field for actual GPU rendition/CPU recovery. `export-enlargement-ui` creates an
original 17x11 PNG with orientation 6, then applies a committed crop through the
real app and exports through UI/MCP before/after restart. Originals, user libraries
and third-party photographs are untouched. These are focused integration fixtures,
not photographic or full-size performance acceptance.

## ACES synthetic reference vectors

`aces-reference.json` contains synthetic numeric results from unmodified ACES 2
CTL at revision `069b0bc3e1f6c62820f19fdae2fecec3f4fc0f80`, adapted independently
to C++ Float64 by `scripts/aces-reference.py`. It records revision and source
hashes, uses no photographs, and is reproducible with
`node scripts/generate-aces-reference.mjs`. The retained reference and license
are in `third_party/aces-core/` (Apache-2.0, Contributors to the ACES Project).

## JPEG gain-map reference vectors

`export-gain-vectors.json` contains original synthetic algebraic reference vectors for an independent Float64 ISO 21496-1 reconstruction oracle. The numeric vectors are dedicated to the public domain under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). They include black offsets, independent channel gains/gamma, partial display headroom and above-white values. No photographic or third-party code content is included. The oracle also reads actual encoded ISO packets and JPEGs independently of the bundled codec; see `tests/export-reference.ts` and `export-rendering.spec.ts`.
